blocks.text: I can use multiplication and division to calculate unknown values in ratio problems.
In this lesson you will decide which multiplication or division equation solves a ratio problem, and then use ratio tables to find missing values.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: A ratio shows the relative sizes of 2 or more values and allows you to compare a part with another part in a whole.
For every allows you to talk about the relative sizes of the values, e.g. for every 2 squares there is 1 triangle.

blocks.text: Each quiz team has 2 adults and 3 children, so 5 people. Here are 3 teams, one team in each row of an array:

rows.note: Adults: 2 in one team × 3 teams = 6 adults.
Children: 3 in one team × 3 teams = 9 children.
People: 5 in one team × 3 teams = 15 people.

blocks.text: Look at the equations 2 × 3 = 6, 3 × 3 = 9 and 5 × 3 = 15.

items: The **2** is the number of adults in one team.
The **first 3** (in 3 × 3) is the number of children in one team.
The **5** is the number of people in one whole team.
The **last 3** in every equation is the number of teams taking part.

blocks.text: When you write an equation, be sure you can explain where each number is in the picture, bar model or array.
Each team has 2 adults and 3 children. Look at this equation: 2 × 6 = 12

options: The number of adults in one team
blocks.why: 2 adults in one team × 6 teams = 12 adults, so the 6 is the number of teams.

blocks.text: Sometimes we know the total and need to find the number of teams. Each team has 2 adults and 3 children.

items: 45 people in total: each team has 5 people, so 45 ÷ 5 = 9 teams.
24 adults: each team has 2 adults, so 24 ÷ 2 = 12 teams. Each team has 3 children, so 3 × 12 = 36 children.
24 children: each team has 3 children, so 24 ÷ 3 = 8 teams. Each team has 2 adults, so 2 × 8 = 16 adults.

blocks.text: Divide to find how many teams. Then multiply to find the other value.
Each team has 2 adults and 3 children.

items.q: 35 people take part. How many teams?
18 adults take part. How many teams?
30 children take part. How many adults?
27 children take part. How many teams?

blocks.text: For every cheese and tomato sandwich you need 2 slices of bread, 3 slices of cheese and 4 slices of tomato. Choose the equation that solves each problem.

items.q: How many sandwiches can you make with 40 slices of bread?
How many slices of tomato do you need for 100 sandwiches?
How many sandwiches can you make with 27 slices of cheese?

items: 26 slices of bread: 26 ÷ 2 = 13 sandwiches. That is 13 times as many as 1 sandwich, so 3 × 13 = 39 slices of cheese and 4 × 13 = 52 slices of tomato.
28 slices of tomato: 28 ÷ 4 = 7 sandwiches. Then 3 × 7 = 21 slices of cheese.
25 slices of cheese: 25 ÷ 3 is 8 with 1 left over. You can make 8 sandwiches with 1 slice of cheese left over.

blocks.text: Aisha and Alex share marbles. For every 2 marbles Aisha has, Alex has 3 marbles.
Aisha always has a multiple of 2, Alex always has a multiple of 3, and the total is always a multiple of 5. Look for the multiplication links in the table.

blocks.q: Match each problem to the column of the table you start from.

pairs.a: They share 20 marbles. How many does Aisha get?
Aisha gets 8 marbles. How many does Alex get?
Alex gets 12 marbles. How many marbles altogether?

blocks.text: If Aisha gets 18 marbles, how many does Alex get, and how many marbles are shared altogether?
In the basic ratio Aisha has 2 marbles. 18 = 2 × 9, so Aisha has 9 times as many marbles. So there must be 9 times as many for Alex and 9 times as many altogether.

rows.note: Alex: 3 marbles in the basic ratio × 9 = 27 marbles.
Total: 5 marbles in the basic ratio × 9 = 45 marbles.

blocks.text: For every 2 marbles Aisha has, Alex has 3 marbles.

blocks.q: Use the table to work out each missing number.

items.q: They share 35 marbles. How many does Alex get?
Aisha gets 16 marbles. How many does Alex get?
Alex gets 24 marbles. How many does Aisha get?
Alex gets 27 marbles. How many marbles altogether?

blocks.text: Aisha uses this recipe to make 12 pancakes: 2 eggs, 3 spoons of sugar and 6 spoons of flour.
**Problem:** Aisha and 3 friends want 6 pancakes each. How much sugar? 4 people × 6 = 24 pancakes. 24 is 2 times as many as 12, so she needs 2 times as much sugar: 2 × 3 = 6 spoons.
**Problem:** Aisha has 12 eggs. How much flour? 12 eggs is 6 times as many as 2, so she needs 6 times as much flour: 6 × 6 = 36 spoons.
**Problem:** 300 pancakes are needed. How many eggs? 300 ÷ 12 = 25, so she needs 25 times as much: 25 × 2 = 50 eggs.

blocks.label: What do the two 6s mean in 6 × 6 = 36?
blocks.text: The first 6 is how many times as many eggs there are (12 eggs is 6 times 2). The second 6 is the spoons of flour in the recipe.
The recipe makes 12 pancakes with 2 eggs, 3 spoons of sugar and 6 spoons of flour.

items.q: How many spoons of flour for 24 pancakes?
How many spoons of sugar for 60 pancakes?
How many pancakes can you make with 9 spoons of sugar?

slides.title: Use multiplication and division to calculate unknown values in ratio problems

items: Ratio tables show the multiplicative relationship between the variables.
Different representations (bar models, arrays, tables) can show the same mathematical structure.
You can use multiplication and division to represent ratio problems and to solve problems with missing values.
Say how many times as many there are, then multiply every value in the ratio by that amount.
